newsitem.title: USA: Futures group says Greenspan remarks significant.
newsitem.headline: Futures group says Greenspan remarks significant.

text.p: Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's comments Friday urging caution on regulating derivatives were significant and may affect lawmakers' decisions when considering related legislation, a futures association executive said.

"If you're going to vote on these issues and you've been kind of on the fence with respect to pro-market or expansion of CFTC (Commodity Futures Trading Commission) power, etcetera, I have to believe that his comments influence that person who's on the fence," John Frawley, chairman of the Managed Futures Association, said.
"So if you're looking for a Good Housekeeping seal of approval, he just sort of stamped it on those who are looking for such a thing," Frawley told reporters at a briefing.
Greenspan at a conference in Florida said congressional efforts to reform regulation of derivatives under the Commodity Exchange Act have raised contentious issues.

The Fed chairman concluded: "The application of the Commodity Exchange Act to off-exchange transactions between institutions seems wholly unnecessary -- private market regulation appears to be achieving public policy objectives quite effectively and efficiently."

Senate Agriculture Committee Chairman Richard Lugar, a Republican from Indiana, and Democratic Senators Tom Harkin of Iowa and Pat Leahy of Vermont, this month introduced a bill to update the Commodity Exchange Act.

"I am really encouraged to see Greenspan's comments because I think they're right on point saying these markets are doing very well on a self-regulatory basis," Robert Easton, chairman of the Managed Futures Association's government relations committee, said.

The association has advocated that the so-called "Treasury Amendment" of the 1974 Commodity Exchange Act should make clear that "professional participants in the over-the-counter markets should be exempted from the vast panoply of regulatory issues that would normally be the jurisdiction of the CFTC," Easton said.

"I think we find his (Greenspan's) comment a very big push from a strong direction towards making this part of the bill become effective as it would remove the cloud that we've had over the years in trading these over the counter markets," Easton said.

The "Treasury Amendment" says transactions in foreign currency, security warrants, repurchase options, government securities and a few other items are exempt from the Commodity Exchange Act unless they involve sale for future delivery conducted on a board of trade.

The Lugar-Harkin-Leahy bill would amend the "Treasury Amendment" to clarify the CFTC's authority to police foreign currency futures and options traded off-exchange in the United States and sold to retail investors by entities that are not otherwise federally regulated.
